outcome: Prevalence of asthma exacerbations during pregnancy
cohort: Pregnant asthmatic women attending a tertiary hospital antenatal clinic were recruited, with outcomes compared between those recruited before (n=89) and after (n=80) the introduction of an antenatal asthma management service.
finding: The introduction of an antenatal asthma management service (AMS) was associated with reduced relative risks for asthma exacerbations, loss of control, and persistent uncontrolled asthma during pregnancy.
